about: Millbrook Vineyards & Winery sits on a 130-acre former dairy farm in Dutchess County, about two hours north of Manhattan. John Dyson, a Millbrook native and Cornell graduate who later served in New York State government, bought the farm in 1982, planted vines the next year with his brother-in-law David Bova, and released the first vintage in 1985. Encouraged by Dr. Konstantin Frank, the Finger Lakes pioneer, he bet on European vinifera grapes when few believed they could survive Hudson Valley winters.

The estate vineyard covers some 30 acres of southwest-facing, gravelly slopes at about 800 feet, and Chardonnay is its largest planting. The Proprietor’s Special Reserve is the winery’s barrel-aged tier, labelled Hudson River Region. Longtime winemaker John Graziano favoured balance over heavy oak, and the reserve Chardonnay has traditionally spent around ten months in three- and four-year-old French barrels, so the wood shapes the texture without dominating. Ian Beaurup now leads the cellar.

Millbrook describes the 2021 as showing vanilla, tangerine, caramel and pear, with forward fruit, integrated oak and bright acidity leading to a clean finish. It is a style that reflects the Hudson Valley’s cool climate: ripe fruit balanced by natural acidity, with oak used as a seasoning rather than the main event. As one of the region’s founding estates, Millbrook helped prove that Chardonnay could thrive this far north.
